newsitem.title: USA: US CREDIT MKT OUTLOOK - Bullish feeling perseveres.
newsitem.headline: US CREDIT MKT OUTLOOK - Bullish feeling perseveres.

text.p: U.S. credit markets will likely keep rolling on Thursday as a pleasant combination of bullish technicals and encouraging fundamentals continue to lure players into fixed-income assets, analysts said.

"There are several technical factors sort of feeding the bullish psychology ... and there is the fundamental backdrop of a very stable expansion," said Lee Youngdahl, bond market analyst and economist at Aubrey G. Lanston and Co Inc.
Analysts said the slew of fresh economic data to be released on Thursday was unlikely to alter the market's underlying bullish sentiment.
"We don't see any big barriers on Thursday ... it seems that I can't go wrong calling for more gains tomorrow," said James Padinha, economist at consulting firm Briefing.com.
Players will start the day with the long-awaited release of the first official estimate for the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) for the second quarter.

The report is due out at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT and Wall Street pundits expect it to show the economy expanded by 1.9 percent in the second three months of the year against a neck-breaking 5.9 percent growth in the first quarter.
The market will also take in the jobless claims report for the week ended July 26. Players see claims rising to 306,000 against 299,000 in the previous week.

Players will as well learn the outcome of the Purchasing Management Association of Chicago July manufacturing survey. Experts see the Chicagoland Business Barometer sliding briefly to 59.8 from 61.5 in June.
A batch of second-tier data, including the APICS business outlook survey for July, is also slated to be announced during Thursday's trading session.
Analysts said fundamentals are likely to continue to underpin the market as long as consumer demand remains on hold and inflation continues to slumber.

"There are two reasons why (recent rises) in production don't affect people. The first one is that demand hasn't shown a concerted rebound yet, and the second reason is there is no inflation," Padinha said.
A large majority of market players believe the Federal Reserve will likely keep monetary policy on hold in the near future. Federal funds are currently targeted at 5.50 percent by the central bank.

Looking at the technical side, analysts said the market has entered a positive cycle. They said money, fund and portfolio managers have been tapping the market in an effort to keep profitability and meet performance targets.
Also, a flood of money has been flowing in from operations involving the selling of mortgage backed securities and the purchase of mid-curve Treasury assets.
"There is a bevy of market participants that have found themselves ... forced to jump on the bandwagon," said a money trader at a major investment bank here.

"There is just a certain performance that has to be met by fund managers, money managers, portfolio managers so the market continues to rise. They have to keep up with the market's performance," the trader added.
In late Wednesday trading, the 6.625-percent benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond was quoted up 29/32 at 104-1/32 to yield 6.32 percent, the lowest level since February 16.
The federal funds rate is expected to open at 5.75 percent on Thursday, well above the Fed's target.
